chapter_meta_description: Li Huowang endures a skin-peeling ritual to forge a substitute talisman, then fuses with Li Sui in a terrifying new power-up. Chapter 517 of Dao Gui Yi Xian.
og_title: The Substitute Talisman and the Daughter Within
og_description: Li Huowang delves into body horror to create a life-saving talisman and a symbiotic fusion with his adoptive daughter. Chapter 517.
twitter_title: Skin off, power on—Li Huowang's latest upgrade is not for the faint of heart.
twitter_description: Li Huowang uses mercury to peel his own skin, then fuses his body with Li Sui to become a tentacled, sword-wielding nightmare.

lore_anchors.definition: A magical artifact that takes a fatal blow for the user. In the Dao-Twisted World, Li Huowang must physically peel his own skin to create one from his Heart-Element flesh.
A heavy metal used in Daoist external alchemy and as a preservative. Here it is used to preserve the peeled skin during the talisman-crafting process.
An internal spirit formed in advanced cultivation. The Luo Sect uses it to boost power; Li Huowang adapts the concept by fusing with Li Sui’s physical tentacles.
A powerful “military path” weapon that corrupts the wielder with bloodlust. Li Huowang wields it while Li Sui controls the Bronze Coin Sword.
A ritual Daoist weapon made of coins strung on red cord. In the Dao-Twisted World, it can scatter and reform as a tactical combat tool.
A healing text of the Ao-Jing Sect that uses a fire-slug to seal wounds. It saved Li Huowang from the skin-peeling but leaves him in lingering pain.
